chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the man who hoards food and waits for it [to raise prices]. Is that permissible? He said: If the food is abundant, sufficient for the people, then there is no problem with it; and if the food is scarce, not sufficient for the people, then it is disliked that he hoards the food and leaves the people with no food.

key_terms.يَحْتَكِرُ: He hoards (monopolizes goods to raise prices)
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: It is disliked (makruh, a recommended but not obligatory prohibition in fiqh)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hoarding food when supplies are scarce versus abundant?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of ihtikar (hoarding) based on the impact on public supply rather than a blanket prohibition. It reflects the Shia juristic view that scarcity triggers makrih (dislike/preference against) to prevent harm to the community, aligning with the broader Islamic economic ethic of ensuring food security and preventing artificial price inflation through strategic withholding.
